title: Metric-led prefetch safety pipeline and AB visualizations for batching configs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a metric-driven pipeline that safely experiments with prefetch and batching config variants, automatically applies safe config changes, and surfaces intuitive A/B visualizations for engineers and product owners. This ticket covers experiment design, telemetry definitions, statistical decision rules, automated rollout/rollback logic, and a set of lightweight dashboards for day-to-day monitoring and postmortem analysis.
background_and_rationale: We have recurring opportunities to reduce per-token cost via prefetch and dynamic minibatching, but past experiments were either too conservative (slow ROI) or too aggressive (incidental latency/quality regressions). This initiative builds a repeatable, conservative safety funnel that: 1) evaluates economic and QoS trade-offs using robust metrics, 2) applies changes automatically only when rules are satisfied, and 3) presents results in a single pane for cross-functional review. Different from previous AB frameworks, this pipeline uses sequential decision rules with traffic-weighted significance and difference-in-differences for controlling drift.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible experiment template that can spin up prefetch/batching config variants and route split traffic (1/5/20%) via feature flags
A telemetry contract listing primary/secondary metrics and thresholds for automated gating
A rollout engine implementation that advances traffic only when statistical gates pass and triggers rollback otherwise
Datadog/Looker dashboards with cohorted A/B visualizations and per-cohort cost and quality deltas
Automation tests + a smoke test that runs a 1% traffic dry-run in staging and validates rollback triggers
statistical_decision_rules: Use a sequential testing approach with alpha-spending (default alpha=0.05) and minimum detectable effect set at 2% relative cost reduction. For latency and quality we use one-sided safety tests: require p95_latency not to increase by >5% (non-inferiority) and quality_eval_score_delta >= -0.2 points. Use difference-in-differences to control for daily traffic drift and bootstrap-based CIs for percentiles. When traffic is low, use Bayesian credible intervals with skeptical priors to avoid noisy early rollouts.
rollout_and_rollback_policy: Start at 1% traffic for 2 hours. If all safety gates pass, advance to 5% for 6 hours, then 20% for 12 hours, then full. Safety gates evaluated at each step: cost improvement >= configured MDE, p95_latency change within non-inferiority margin, quality eval no regression beyond threshold, error and fallback rates below tolerances. Any gate fail triggers immediate rollback to previous stable config and an SLO alert to #runtime-oncall. All automatic rollbacks create a GitHub issue and post a runbook link in the incident channel.
dashboards_and_visuals: A cohort timeline view showing cost delta, p95 latency delta, and quality delta over experiment steps
A split-by-customer-tier view (free, standard, enterprise) to spot segmentation effects
A sequential decision log panel that marks gating checks and pass/fail reasons
A heatmap of per-route token-economics to avoid applying aggressive configs on high-value routes
A compact experiment summary card for the Console rollout UI with link to telemetry and PRs
implementation_notes:
- Reuse feature-flagging infra to route split traffic and annotate traces with experiment_id.
- Implement gating service as a lightweight orchestrator invoked by rollout controller; keep state in Redis for short-lived experiments.
- Use existing prefix/KV cache metrics emitted by the runtime and extend with per-experiment tags.
- Add experiment metadata to trace spans for correlation in distributed tracing.
- Keep hard-coded thresholds configurable in a managed YAML so SRE/product can tune without deploys.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for gate evaluation logic (edge cases: zero traffic, NaNs). 2) Integration tests that mock telemetry and assert the controller advances/rolls back correctly. 3) Staging smoke run: 1% split for 2 hours with synthetic traffic including corner cases (long sequences, short sequences, batched vs single). 4) Canary in prod with low-traffic customer cohort and manual human-in-the-loop approval before 20% stage.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overfitting to synthetic eval sets -> Mitigation: require both eval-set pass and production-sampled quality metric aligned before advancing
Risk: Metric alerts noisy at low traffic -> Mitigation: use Bayesian smoothing and require consistency across two consecutive windows
Risk: Unexpected tail-latency regressions on specific routes -> Mitigation: route-based heatmap and immediate per-route rollback capability
Risk: Cost savings concentrated on low-value routes leading to revenue harm -> Mitigation: annotate routes with revenue-sensitivity and block aggressive configs on tier=enterprise
updates: 2025-02-14: Ticket created by Aisha. Initial scoping and goals captured.
2025-02-20: Design review with Lina Ortega; agreed to use difference-in-differences and bootstrap CI for percentile metrics.
2025-02-27: Prototype gating service merged (PR referenced). Added experiment_id tags to runtime metrics. (Markus)
2025-03-03: First staging smoke run completed; observed noisy p99 with synthetic bursts. Decided to hold p99 as secondary metric and rely primarily on p95 for gating.
2025-03-07: Dashboards wireframe complete; UX review scheduled with PM. Added revenue-sensitivity annotation to routes dataset.
2025-03-10: Began a limited prod canary on internal dev tenants at 1% traffic. Observed 3.1% cost improvement, p95 change +0.8% (within non-inferiority). Continuing to 5% if stable for 6 hours.
